title: Boston Scientific downgraded at JP Morgan as new negatives to impact shares - TradingView
content: JP Morgan downgraded Boston Scientific BSX to neutral from overweight on Wednesday, saying the medical device company is facing several new negative factors that will weigh on shares. The bank cut its price target to $46 from $56 (~8% upside based on Wednesday's close). Analyst Robbie Marcus said key headwinds are additional earnings projection downgrades, China pricing, Penumbra close timing and financing rates, negative 2027 sales and EPS growth guidance. And "the most concerning, in our view, [is] an almost across-the-board pushout in unrelated key pipeline programs. Marcus' note came out the same day that Boston Scientific cut its 2026 outlook, citing the impact from an August cybersecurity incident. Shares closed off 6%. "But now with the fourth quarter in a row where forward estimates are moving lower, in this case due to new negatives primarily, we just don't see how a near-term stabilization in either fundamentals or sentiment is possible," Marcus wrote. "Too much is moving in the wrong direction at the same time still, meaning we can't envision much of a near-term recovery anytime soon and expect shares to mostly trade sideways until further notice."DisclaimerContent provided by Seeking Alpha is intended for information purposes only, and that Seeking Alpha does not offer any personalist investment advice and is not a licensed securities dealer, broker, US investment adviser or investment bank. The My OnChain Net Yield Fund (MONY) and the JPMorgan OnChain Liquidity–Token Money Market Fund (JLTXX) are now available on Solana to qualified investors in the US, adding a second public network to the firm's tokenised cash management platform alongside Ethereum. The two funds serve different investor needs. MONY is a 506(c) private placement fund that allows qualified investors to earn US dollar yields. J.P. Morgan Asset Management launched MONY on the public Ethereum blockchain on 15 December 2025, using Kinexys Digital Assets, the firm's asset tokenisation solution. JLTXX is a US registered government money market fund designed to invest in a way that supports stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act, the US federal stablecoin law enacted in July 2025. The fund launched on Ethereum on 13 May 2026, investing only in US Treasury securities and overnight repurchase agreements. At launch, J.P. Morgan Asset Management invested USD 100 million in the fund, with additional participation from Anchorage Digital. Investors access both funds through Morgan Money, J.P. Morgan Asset Management's open-architecture trading and analytics platform for liquidity management. Through a single platform, qualified investors can subscribe to and redeem from the tokenised funds and receive token balances at their blockchain addresses. The firm says this gives clients a consistent experience as they extend tokenised activity across several networks. Paul Przybylski, Global Head of Product, Digital & Tokenized Assets at J.P. Morgan Asset Management, said clients operate across more than one network and their liquidity should do the same. He added that bringing JLTXX and MONY to Solana gives stablecoin issuers and institutional investors access to the same funds on the onchain networks where they operate, and supports the firm's plans to scale tokenised cash management through multi-chain channels. The Solana launch moves the funds beyond Ethereum for the first time. For stablecoin issuers that hold or operate tokens on Solana, the expansion means a GENIUS Act-oriented reserve fund is now available on the same network. For institutional investors, it adds another chain on which they can hold tokenised money market fund shares without leaving the Morgan Money platform. The dual mandate on what are shaping up to be the two largest IPOs of 2026 is notable not just for the fees involved — estimated at roughly $84 million in direct underwriting revenue on Anthropic alone — but because CEO Jamie Dimon is personally expected to help market both deals, a level of executive involvement that underscores how aggressively the bank is defending a competitive moat rivals will struggle to replicate. During the SpaceX (SPCX) listing, Dimon conducted a live Q&A session with Elon Musk that helped generate over $100 billion in individual investor demand — a staggering figure that effectively proved the viability of mass-scale retail allocations in trillion-dollar offerings. Anthropic is considering a retail allocation of approximately 15% to 20% of total shares on offer, with JPMorgan expected to coordinate outreach to high-net-worth individuals, private banking clients, and broker platforms. Analyst estimates suggest the Anthropic IPO could generate a total equity capital markets fee pool of roughly $562 million, with JPMorgan's $84 million share capturing only the direct underwriting component — not the ancillary revenue from wealth management relationships and trading commissions tied to the retail tranche. Goldman Sachs (GS) and Morgan Stanley (MS) hold the lead-left and lead-right underwriting positions on both deals, respectively, yet JPMorgan's retail distribution franchise arguably touches more individual investors than either bookrunner. The Anthropic deal does present distinct marketing challenges compared to SpaceX, because CEO Dario Amodei — while respected in the AI research community — lacks the cultural magnetism of Elon Musk and does not generate the same retail investor fervor. That reality is expected to shift JPMorgan's strategy toward leveraging Dimon's own stature and credibility with ultra-high-net-worth clients rather than relying on founder celebrity appeal. title: JP Morgan lashes out at ‘unprincipled’ bank tax - The Telegraph
content: Wall Street giant criticises John Healey’s Budget announcement on surcharge increase Tom Saunders is The Telegraph's Financial Correspondent. He was named one of MHP's 30 To Watch young journalists and won the European Parliament's Daphne Caruana Galizia prize for journalism. He previously worked as a business reporter at The Times. Email him at tom.saunders@telegraph.co.uk or find him on X @tomjs Tom Saunders is The Telegraph's Financial Correspondent. He was named one of MHP's 30 To Watch young journalists and won the European Parliament's Daphne Caruana Galizia prize for journalism. He previously worked as a business reporter at The Times. Email him at tom.saunders@telegraph.co.uk or find him on X @tomjs JP Morgan has criticised John Healey’s tax raid on banks, saying it “lacks principle”. The Wall Street bank said it was unfair for the Chancellor to “single out” banks after Mr Healey announced an increase in the surcharge on bank profits in the Budget. JP Morgan reportedly faces paying an additional £100m to £150m because of the higher surcharge. It has paid £5.5bn in bank-specific taxes since 2011. Mr Healey will temporarily double the surcharge from 3pc to 6pc for 15 months from January to provide “immediate support on energy bills”, he said. The surcharge is levied in addition to the top rate of corporation tax, which now stands at 25pc, bringing the total rate faced by the sector to 31pc – the highest level since at least 2015. The Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) estimates that the higher tax rate will bring in an extra £1.5bn, though it believes that roughly £190m of UK profits would move out of the UK following the rise in tax. Responding to the Budget announcement, a JP Morgan spokesman said the bank was “committed” to the UK and recognised the cost of living challenges facing the country. But they added: “To single out this industry for additional taxes again, one of the UK’s biggest generators of growth and jobs, lacks principle. “It also overlooks that the banking industry operates in a highly competitive global marketplace.” International banks, including JP Morgan and Citi, have been among the most high-profile critics of increasing bank taxes, warning that it could drive investment and jobs abroad. Jamie Dimon, JP Morgan’s chief executive, has been amongst the staunchest critics of the policy. In July, he said there would be “adverse consequences” if Andy Burnham targeted lenders with fresh windfall taxes to help fund his spending plans. “I always thought it was wrong. We’re a great citizen [in the UK]. We hire people there. We want to be bigger there. We train people there. We hire veterans there,” he said. “So if a government decides to do it, there’s nothing I can do, but it will over time cause decisions made that they may not like.” Much of the City had feared that the Chancellor would raise the bank surcharge to 8pc, where it had sat until Jeremy Hunt, the then Conservative chancellor, lowered it to 3pc in 2023. News of Mr Healey’s plans leaked to Bloomberg hours before he announced them in Parliament, which led bank shares to rally. Dame Meg Hillier, the chairman of the Treasury committee, wrote to the Treasury and Financial Conduct Authority demanding answers over the leak, which she said was “deeply concerning”. Bank shares rallied further on confirmation that the increase would be smaller than expected and time-limited. Barclays rose by 3.2pc, while Lloyds Bank and NatWest were both up closer to 4pc. Lloyds Bank and NatWest are the most exposed to any rise in the bank tax, according to Gary Greenwood, an analyst at Shorecap, with Barclays slightly less affected. HSBC and Standard Chartered, which make much of their money overseas, are even less exposed to the tax increase. The reprieve on bank taxes was one of the few good pieces of news in the Budget for the City, which was explicitly aimed at giving families and businesses “breathing space”. The Budget had a number of other measures focused on “bloody minded entrepreneurs”, as Mr Healey termed them, but not all of them were positive. Founders’ relief for capital gains tax will offer them a reduced 10pc rate when selling their businesses. However, tax analysts said the criteria for achieving the relief were so narrow that very few founders would qualify. Nimesh Shah, the chief executive of Blick Rothenberg, the tax consultancy, said it was “very narrow in scope and many successful owner-managed businesses are unlikely to qualify”. At the same time, the more widely used business asset disposal relief has been made less generous. The threshold for tax relief was cut from £1m to £500,000. The Chancellor said that he would increase the generosity of tax-advantaged employee share option schemes. The Government has also overhauled the way businesses can write off the costs of equipment against their tax bills, slowing the rate at which businesses can offset the cost of equipment against their tax bills while offering a bigger upfront write-off on some new investment. Ultimately, the policy will raise £1bn for the Treasury.

title: Nigeria too important for global banks to ignore, says JP Morgan - Peoples Gazette Nigeria
content: JP Morgan’s decision to expand operations in Nigeria shows confidence in recent economic reforms and the quality of banking regulation, its West Africa managing director says. JP Morgan’s decision to expand its operations in Nigeria shows its confidence in recent economic reforms and the quality of banking regulation, the lender’s West Africa managing director, Dapo Olagunju, says. Mr Olagunju said the U.S. bank saw opportunities in Nigeria despite reports of multinational companies leaving the country, arguing that those departures did not reflect the full investment environment. He spoke during a panel discussion at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit in Abuja on Tuesday. His comments followed the Central Bank of Nigeria’s recent approval-in-principle for the establishment of JPMorgan Merchant Bank Nigeria Limited. The preliminary approval advances the lender’s expansion plans but does not authorise it to begin banking operations. Mr Olagunju said the bank could have retained its representative office without seeking a banking licence, but its assessment of the reforms and regulatory environment encouraged a deeper commitment. “We think that the central bank is very well professionally run at this time,” he said. title: JP Morgan slams Healey for bank tax hike that ‘lacks principle’ - City AM
content: JP Morgan has slammed the Labour government for raising taxes on the UK banking sector and said the move “lacks principle”. Wall Street’s biggest bank, which serves over 2.5m UK users through its retail arm Chase, said it is “committed” to the UK but raised concern over the targeting of the sector in John Healey’s first Budget. “To single out this industry for additional taxes again, one of the UK’s biggest generators of growth and jobs, lacks principle,” a spokesperson for the bank said. “It also overlooks that the banking industry operates in a highly competitive global marketplace.” Healey doubled the UK banking surcharge, which sits on top of corporation tax, to six per cent to fund an energy support package. The increase will last 15 months and is expected to raise an extra £1.5bn. Three daily briefings with the key market moves and top business and political stories. British banking stocks rallied following the Budget after the surcharge increase under shot previous expectations. It was previously thought that the levy would return to eight per cent, the level it sat at in 2023. A banking sector source said there’s “disappointment” given the tax hike doesn’t signal support for the sector, though added many had gone into the day “thinking it could have been worse”. Healey said he “celebrates” and was “grateful” for banks but was asking them to “help fund breathing space for British families”. The Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) said “some banks are assumed to move profits out of the UK in response to the higher tax rate,” adding the overall size of this was “uncertain”. It pencilled in around £190m of profit shifting overseas in its economic outlook. JP Morgan employs around 23,000 people across the UK and has major hubs in London and Bournemouth. Last year, the US giant unveiled plans for a £3bn mega tower in Canary Wharf that would serve as its new London headquarters. The 3m square feet tower in London is expected to inject as much as £10bn over the next six years into the local economy. But the bank’s boss Jamie Dimon had previously warned the tower could be reconsidered if the government turned “hostile” towards banks. He later added sector-specific taxes have “adverse consequences”. Dimon’s Wall Street peer Citibank boss Dame Jane Fraser previously sounded the alarm on a bank tax, warning “money votes with its feet”. The tax increase is directly earmarked in the Budget papers to Healey’s plan for a £100 “household energy payment” to 20m households in council tax banks A-D. David Postings, chief executive of trade body UK Finance, said increasing bank taxes was “not, in our view, the best way to deliver growth”. “The Chancellor’s promise that this increase will be time-limited is therefore important, given we already have a tax regime that needs to be made more internationally competitive.” Will Howlett, financials analyst at Quilter Cheviot, said the time limit on the levy increase “should be taken with a pinch of salt”. “The geopolitical situation shows no sign of abating and given much of this windfall is going to help lower income households, there will need to be a material change to the conflict in the Middle East for the better in order for the government to feel they can return to the previous levels.” Subscribe to the City AM newsletter to have our top stories delivered directly to your inbox. (“the Company” or “GT Metabolic”), a pioneer in the medical device field and the first to receive FDA De Novo grant and 510(k) clearance for use of magnetic technology to create compression anastomoses (connections between two tubular structures in the body, such as intestines), today announced a Series C growth investment from J.P. Morgan Life Sciences Private Capital. Proceeds from the financing will support the Company’s ongoing global commercial launch and fund expansion into new surgical and therapeutic settings, with endoscopic and colorectal surgery next with additional indications to follow. GT Metabolic’s novel linear magnetic anastomosis system provides an incisionless, sutureless, staple-free, and reversable technique for the creation of gastrointestinal (GI) compression anastomoses. The approach results in fully patent anastomoses without leaving foreign material in the body that could impede the healing process – a key differentiator against standard of care. Further, the Company’s device can be used regardless of the surgical access employed by the operating physician, be it endoscopic, robotic, or laparoscopic. Each year, up to 18% of GI anastomotic procedures result in life-threatening complications such as leaks and bleeding that often can result in acute outcomes such as sepsis, hospital readmission, and death. GT’s linear magnetic system uses magnetic compression for the formation of seamless, innate-biology-preserving anastomoses, with the potential to reduce complication rates without sacrificing efficacy. “The use of magnets in surgery is a game-changing technology to address serious adverse events, such as leaks and bleeding, which have troubled surgeons since the advent of minimally invasive surgery over 50 years ago,” said Joe Siletto, Managing Partner at J.P. Morgan Life Sciences Private Capital. “Over the past 20 years, the Company’s co-founder and CMO, Dr. Michel Gagner, has vigilantly pursued the use of magnets to provide surgeons with a superior solution for anastomosis creation; his mission has always been to reduce surgical complications and improve patient outcomes.” “J.P. Morgan Life Sciences Private Capital’s growth investment will help accelerate both product development, surgeon trainings and worldwide commercial expansion,” said Thierry Thaure, co-founder and CEO of GT Metabolic. “This is an important milestone for GT Metabolic as we advance additional paradigm-shifting anastomotic products and work to deliver improved care for patients.” “We are proud to partner with GT Metabolic as it works to transform minimally invasive surgical care,” said Anthony Perry, Vice President at J.P. Morgan Life Sciences Private Capital. “With authorizations for anastomosis in a number of surgical procedures across the U.S., Europe, South America and other regions, our team is excited to provide GT with the financial support to bolster its commercialization efforts, further invest in additional anastomosis indications such as for use in colorectal surgery, and expand patient and provider access to these novel products.” J.P. Morgan Life Sciences Private Capital’s investment marks GT Metabolic’s first institutional financing partnership and is the fifth investment made by the J.P. Morgan Life Sciences Private Capital team. This partnership underscores J.P. Morgan’s commitment to partnering with founders and founder-owned businesses, providing the strategic capital and support needed to empower innovative companies to scale and realize their full potential. GT Metabolic Solutions is a medical device company that develops and manufactures magnetic compression products designed for the safer creation of gastrointestinal anastomoses. With locations in Minneapolis, Minnesota, San Jose, California, and Montréal, Canada, GT Metabolic’s products have demonstrated efficacy in reliably creating anastomoses while driving low complication rates to reduce the need for surgical re-interventions. title: Alpaca, Citi, JP Morgan among early adopters as DTCC Tokenization Service goes live - Ledger Insights
content: Today the DTCC launched its Tokenization Service after the SEC granted a no-action letter in December 2025. At launch just 34 securities are eligible, a mix of equities, Treasuries and ETFs. The SEC’s no-action letter covers a far broader set, the full Russell 1000, US Treasuries and major index ETFs, worth roughly $30 trillion of the more than $114 trillion DTC holds in custody. These are tokenized entitlements that carry the same ownership rights as conventional securities held in street name at DTC and share the same CUSIP. A key goal is 24/7 transfers. When a tokenized position moves between registered wallets, that is the settlement, so there is no T+1 wait. However, there are limits in the early period. Moving a token between chains goes through DTC’s conversion service, which runs from 2am to 6pm ET on business days, so round the clock transfers are intrachain only. The same service converts positions between conventional and tokenized form. Transfers can only be made between registered wallets. DTC Participants can register selected third party wallets for their clients via a user interface. Twenty DTC Participants have signed up so far. They include global banks and custodians such as JP Morgan, Citi, Bank of America, Barclays, BNP Paribas, UBS, Morgan Stanley and State Street, retail and clearing brokers including Fidelity, Edward Jones, Apex, DriveWealth and Clear Street, and crypto adjacent firms Alpaca and Velocity Capital. Notable absences are BNY, the largest custodian, and Goldman Sachs, which took part in the July live trials. Future users will be onboarded on a rolling basis. There’s a misconception that tokenization is only happening on the Canton Network. DTC’s Besu-based private distributed ledger is also available at launch and provides the foundation for the DTCC Collateral AppChain due early next year. By then additional networks such as Stellar and Circle’s Arc are expected to join the fray, as well as other blockchains subject to client demand. The roadmap for 2027 and beyond includes expanding the eligible securities and asset servicing. For now settlement arrangements are up to Participants, but given the DTCC group’s critical role in securities settlement it is not surprising that it has plans in this area. Today netting via the NSCC typically reduces the settlement figure for conventional securities by around 98%, and the roadmap includes on-chain cash netting. The DTCC has previously told Ledger Insights it is exploring stablecoins and tokenized deposits for settlement. While not necessarily indicative, JPMorgan played a prominent role in the July live transactions and has said it plans to launch JPM Coin on Canton. Previous DTCC collateral simulations included Société Générale FORGE’s stablecoins and Fnality’s institutional settlement system. It remains to be seen whether use cases will bifurcate, with traditional finance attracted to 24/7 movement of collateral and crypto natives using DTC tokens to trade or to underpin wrapped tokens. Alpaca is among the launch participants and Ondo is named as a collaborator, which points toward wrapped tokens. Trading could happen via ATS venues or tokenized securities venues that are subject to the SEC’s innovation exemption. Canton may not be known as a major DeFi trading venue, but one of the first TSVs planning to launch, TSV LLC, is on the Canton Network. That said, it only plans to support issuer-sponsored tokens rather than third party tokens such as the DTCC’s.

title: NES 32: J.P. Morgan, Chevron seek stronger legal shield for long-term Nigeria bet - Businessday NG
content:
Global investors, including JPMorgan Chase and Chevron, have called for stronger legal guarantees, policy consistency and improved security to sustain Global investors, including JPMorgan Chase and Chevron, have called for stronger legal guarantees, policy consistency and improved security to sustain long-term investments in Nigeria, warning that businesses need predictable rules and competitive operating costs to commit capital. Speaking at a panel session titled “Innovation, Investment and the Next Decade of Partnerships” sponsored by IHS Towers at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit in Abuja on Tuesday, executives said recent economic reforms had improved Nigeria’s investment prospects but stressed that the gains must be backed by durable laws and consistent implementation. Dapo Olagunju, managing director of JPMorgan Chase in Nigeria, said the bank had operated in the country since 1960 and maintained a physical office presence since 1982, adding that it viewed recent reforms and regulatory developments positively. He said the impact of reforms introduced over the past three to four years had been significant, reinforcing the importance of Nigeria to a global financial institution. Read also: Why J.P. Morgan picked these five Nigerians to lead its merchant bank “The last time an international bank opened an office in Nigeria was probably in 2000. And that was when we moved from military dictatorship into civilian democracy. J.P. Morgan coming in at this time also sort of signifies that the impact of the reform that we put in place in the last three or four years is almost at the same level,” he said. For Chevron, which has operated in Nigeria since 1961, the next phase of investment will depend on the stability of the policy environment, security and the competitiveness of project costs. Jim Swartz, chairman and managing director of Chevron Nigeria and Mid-Africa, said the company had investment plans across several projects, including shallow-water operations, Usan, Owowo, Bonga Southwest and infill wells at Agbami. He said the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) and presidential directives had helped make the investment environment more attractive, but sustained investment required long-term laws, improved security, reduced oil theft and timely project delivery. “And so, when you think about all of those, what will it take to sustain the attraction? It’s really the sustained commitment in terms of turning the directives and new legislation into long-term, durable law that we know is going to be there. Because our investments are not only for the near term, and some of these things are infill drilling, near-term results, but multi-decade investments. “Knowing that we will have long-term support in the laws is very important. Knowing that we will have a secure operation is very important. And it’s been very good to see the movement that’s been made in the oil-producing regions of the Delta to improve the security and reduce the loss to oil theft, which has been a major inhibitor to any work there for a long time,” he said. Swartz’s comments underscore the challenge of translating recent policy changes into long-term capital commitments in the oil and gas industry, where projects require substantial funding and years of planning before production and returns. Kendra Gaither, president of the U.S.-Africa Business Centre at the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, said investment decisions depended not only on the opportunities available in a market but also on how easily and fairly businesses could operate. Read also: False identities, dead voters spark controversy over INEC register She identified market access, clear and accessible regulations, transparency, the rule of law, stability, accountability, due process and fair treatment as important considerations for investors. Gaither said Nigeria offered investment opportunities but needed to provide a predictable and transparent environment in which companies could make long-term decisions with confidence. “Companies are looking at where environments are predictable, where there’s transparency, where there’s stability, and where there’s accountability and due process. So is there a reasonable expectation that U.S. companies will be treated fairly and equally to their counterparts here in Nigeria? “Can they expect that not just the rules will be applied fairly, but they’re easy to access and clear to understand and to comply with? If there are disputes, because there are almost always disputes or issues that arise, is there a reasonable expectation that those disputes “Gaither said. The panel also stressed the importance of fiscal credibility and consistency in strengthening investor confidence, particularly as Nigeria seeks to improve its standing in international capital markets. Gaither said Nigeria’s ambition to attain investment-grade status by 2030 was promising but cautioned against using lower risk premiums simply as an opportunity to increase borrowing. Instead, she said Nigeria should improve the structure of its borrowing and demonstrate fiscal responsibility, resilience to external shocks, credibility and consistency. The speaker also identified foreign exchange reforms and the removal of petrol subsidies as measures that had helped improve the country’s investment outlook. Read also: Olukonyinsola Ajayi: From banking reforms to JPMorgan’s Board Beyond the broader policy environment, telecoms operators said the protection of critical infrastructure and the cost of deploying digital networks remained important to attracting investment. Gbenga Adebayo, chairman of the Association of Licensed Telecommunications Operators of Nigeria (ALTON), called for stronger legislation to protect telecommunications and other digital infrastructure designated as critical national assets. He said damage to infrastructure had declined since the government designated it as critical national infrastructure, while enforcement and consequence management had improved. However, he said existing laws and penalties needed to be updated to reflect the importance of the assets being protected. Adebayo also called for the removal of right-of-way charges across all states, warning that inconsistent fees and prohibitive land rents could increase the cost of deploying telecommunications infrastructure. Shuaibu Afolabi, chairman of the Senate Committee on ICT and Cybersecurity, said the 2025 amendment had designated critical national information infrastructure, including telecommunications networks, banking systems and the National Identity Number database. He said the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation was coordinating relevant stakeholders to improve understanding and enforcement of laws governing information and communications technology and cybercrime. Afolabi said the Senate would consider relevant legislation and welcomed contributions from industry stakeholders. Read also: J.P. Morgan’s Nigeria presence signals investor confidence in Tinubu’s reforms – NRS “If we extend this, it will also mean that if you have a data centre somewhere, that the land on which that data centre is built in Lekki, in Victoria Island, should be designated as a critical national asset. We will see how we can resolve the tension between these, and that’s why in the 10th Assembly, particularly the Committee I chair, three things drive our legislative activities. Number one, we’re not legislating for specific technology, we are legislating around principles,” he said. He also emphasised Nigeria’s importance to investors seeking opportunities across the continent. The panel’s discussions highlighted the need for Nigeria to convert reforms into a stable investment framework that can withstand policy changes and give businesses greater certainty over operating costs, regulation and dispute resolution. Investors said predictable regulations, fair treatment, security, ease of doing business and consistent implementation would be crucial to attracting and retaining capital, while the existing U.S.-Nigeria Commercial Investment Partnership could provide a platform for deeper commercial engagement. The next evidence is transaction activity from approved institutions, additional supported use cases, integration with tokenised collateral and disclosures about outages and compliance controls. The latest development in JPM’s corner of the digital-asset market is worth examining beyond the headline. A 2026-10-19 announcement describes a concrete change, but the investment consequences will depend on how it works in practice. The original record is available in the original company statement; here is what it establishes, why the distinction matters and what remains unproven. J.P. Morgan said on October 19 that its JPM Coin deposit token, ticker JPMD, had been brought to Ethereum. The bank describes the service as available to eligible institutional clients, extending a token representing dollar deposits at J.P. Morgan to another public blockchain. It is not an open retail dollar coin anyone can mint or redeem freely. The important development is a major bank connecting its own deposit liabilities with blockchain-based institutional workflows rather than issuing an unrelated speculative crypto asset. A deposit token and an independently issued payment stablecoin can look similar in a wallet interface, but the legal claims and eligible users may be very different. JPM Coin represents money deposited with the bank, subject to its programme terms and access controls. J.P. Morgan has also used the Base network, another Ethereum-compatible environment. The Ethereum expansion therefore increases where approved institutions can move the token without necessarily changing who is permitted to hold it. The bank pointed to Ethereum’s liquidity and existing tokenised-asset activity as a reason for the integration. Large financial institutions are interested in placing cash next to securities on shared infrastructure so that trading, payments and collateral operations can be coordinated. Onchain cash legs may shorten operational handoffs, but legal settlement arrangements and counterparty exposure still matter. An Ethereum transfer being final at the protocol level is not a complete description of a regulated financial transaction. For cryptocurrency investors, the central point is to distinguish an announced milestone from an immediate change in asset value. The underlying development can strengthen a company’s product, legal position or operating capacity without determining what a token will trade for tomorrow. The linked source establishes what was disclosed; the valuation question requires a separate assessment of customers, costs, execution and market conditions. That gap between a confirmed fact and a forecast is where much of the investment risk sits. Running a bank-backed instrument on public networks introduces a deliberate mix of openness and permissioning. Validators and infrastructure may be widely distributed, yet the asset itself can restrict eligible holders and transfer paths. That hybrid design is often more realistic for regulated institutions than assuming all treasury assets must be freely transferable. It also complicates claims that public-chain adoption automatically means universal decentralised access for users. The next evidence is transaction activity from approved institutions, additional supported use cases, integration with tokenised collateral and disclosures about outages and compliance controls. The announcement confirms an Ethereum deployment but does not prove mainstream adoption by every banking customer. It shows how finance is experimenting with common blockchain infrastructure while preserving many of the boundaries and responsibilities of the conventional banking system. Market watchers should also avoid treating a company’s or regulator’s headline as a substitute for terms and conditions. Tokens, shares and regulated service agreements create different rights, even when they coexist in one wallet or platform. A reliable follow-up should ask which entity is responsible, what a holder can actually redeem or transfer, and whether the claimed advantages appear in live activity. According to the company's filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, net earnings were about fifteen point three billion dollars, or five dollars and fifty-seven cents per diluted share, compared with about fourteen point four billion dollars, or five dollars and seven cents per share, in the same quarter a year earlier. JPMorgan Chase is among the companies tracked in our Financial Stocks coverage. The release covered a wide set of businesses. JPMorgan Chase shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange and are tracked by the [Dow Jones Industrial Average], S&P 500, NYSE Composite and Russell 1000. Trading desks produced higher revenue, advisory fees expanded, card balances grew, and assets under management climbed. At the same time, the bank booked a securities loss, added to loan-loss reserves in wholesale lending, and raised its expense guidance for the year. Chairman and Chief Executive Jamie Dimon also used the release to point to a list of macro uncertainties, including fiscal deficits, inflation, elevated asset prices and geopolitical tension. This article walks through the principal figures, explains how each major business contributed, and sets out what the company said about capital and guidance. All figures come from the company's filing and from published reports on the results; where a detail could not be verified, it is described in general terms. The report was released earlier this month, and the figures remain the most recent company-specific reference point as the rest of the large-bank earnings season unfolds. JPMorgan reported net earnings of about fifteen point three billion dollars for the third quarter, up from roughly fourteen point four billion dollars a year earlier. Diluted earnings per share were five dollars and fifty-seven cents, compared with five dollars and seven cents in the prior-year period. Reported revenue was about fifty point two billion dollars, while managed revenue, which adjusts for certain tax-equivalent items, was about fifty point nine billion dollars, an increase of roughly eight percent. The company also presented figures that exclude a securities loss. According to published summaries of the release, the bank recorded a securities portfolio loss of about six hundred fifty-eight million dollars before tax, or roughly four hundred ninety-eight million dollars after tax. Without that item, net earnings would have been about fifteen point eight billion dollars, or five dollars and seventy-five cents per share. Management also reported its earnings rate on tangible common equity. That measure was about twenty percent as reported and about twenty-one percent when the securities loss is excluded. The rate on total common equity was about seventeen percent. These ratios are closely watched in banking because they show how much the firm earns relative to the capital that stock owners have placed behind the business, and JPMorgan has long pointed to them as its main yardstick. Book value per share rose about six percent to roughly one hundred thirty-two dollars, and tangible book value per share rose about seven percent to roughly one hundred thirteen dollars, according to the published summaries. Net interest revenue, the gap between what the bank earns on loans and securities and what it pays on deposits and funding, rose about thirteen percent to roughly twenty-seven point one billion dollars. Excluding the markets business, which carries its own funding dynamics, the figure rose about six percent to roughly twenty-four point seven billion dollars. Average loans were up about ten percent, to roughly one point six trillion dollars, and average deposits grew about eight percent, according to published reports. The company raised its guidance for the full year. Reports on the release said full-year net interest revenue is now expected at about one hundred six point two billion dollars, up from about one hundred five point five billion dollars previously. Net interest revenue excluding markets is expected at about ninety-seven point two billion dollars, compared with about ninety-six point five billion dollars before. The bank also offered a preliminary figure of about one hundred seven billion dollars for that ex-markets measure next year. Guidance of this kind is an expectation, not a result, and it depends on the path of short-term interest rates, deposit behavior and loan demand. A higher figure signals that management sees balance-sheet growth and asset repricing offsetting any pressure from lower short-term rates, but the numbers can shift if the economy or the rate path changes. Adjusted expense guidance was lifted as well, to about one hundred eight point six billion dollars from about one hundred seven point five billion dollars. Management attributed part of the increase to stronger revenue, which tends to bring higher incentive compensation and volume-related costs. Markets revenue was about ten point three billion dollars, up about fifteen percent from a year earlier. The standout was equity markets, where revenue grew about forty-nine percent to roughly five billion dollars. Bond, currency and commodity trading revenue, at about five point four billion dollars, was down about four percent, so the gain was concentrated in one half of the franchise. Strong equity trading at large banks in recent quarters has been associated with elevated client activity, higher volumes in derivatives and financing products, and swings in stock prices that keep clients repositioning. The company's own release attributed the gain to the equities business broadly, and the filing does not break out specific client segments. Peers such as Goldman Sachs also reported a sharp rise in equities revenue for the same period, which points to an industry-wide pattern rather than a single-firm event. Trading revenue can be volatile. A quarter of heavy client activity may be followed by a quieter period, and the decline in bond and currency trading shows that not every desk benefits from the same conditions. Market participants following the stock therefore tend to look at trading results alongside more recurring lines such as net interest revenue, card fees and asset management fees to judge how steady the overall earnings base is. The firm also noted that net interest revenue tied to markets grew, which links the trading desk's balance-sheet use to the bank's headline interest figures. Fee revenue from advisory and underwriting, which the bank reports under its banking line, was about three billion dollars, up about fourteen percent. Total revenue for the banking business was about three point one billion dollars, up about fifteen percent, mainly on higher advisory fees. Published reports cited a year-to-date global fee share of about nine point two percent through September. Advisory revenue reflects completed mergers and acquisitions, and its rise is consistent with a busier deal calendar across the industry this year. Large banks have said that deal conversations broadened as financing conditions became easier and corporate boards grew more comfortable with price levels, although completion timing still depends on regulatory reviews and market conditions. The commercial and corporate banking segment, which houses the markets and banking businesses along with payments and securities services, reported revenue of about twenty-two point seven billion dollars, up about fourteen percent, and net earnings of about eight point two billion dollars, up about twenty percent. Payments revenue was about five point six billion dollars, up about fourteen percent. It is worth noting that fee revenue of this kind depends on corporate confidence. If market volatility rises or financing costs move sharply, boards can postpone transactions. The company's release does not give a dollar figure for its pipeline, so the durability of the fee strength in coming quarters remains an open question. Consumer and Community Banking reported revenue of about twenty-one point two billion dollars, up about nine percent, and net earnings of about five point seven billion dollars, up about thirteen percent. Within that segment, card services and auto revenue was about eight point three billion dollars, up about fifteen percent, helped by higher card balances, a stronger net yield and auto operating lease revenue. Debit and credit card sales volume grew about ten percent. Asset and Wealth Management produced revenue of about six point nine billion dollars, up about fourteen percent, and net earnings of about one point eight billion dollars, up about eleven percent. Assets under management reached about five point two trillion dollars, up about thirteen percent, while client assets were about seven point nine trillion dollars, up about fifteen percent. Net inflows of client assets were roughly two hundred sixty-three billion dollars over the period. These businesses matter because they tend to be steadier than trading. Card balances generate interest and fees as long as consumers keep borrowing and repaying, while wealth management fees rise with asset values and new client money. The same features also create exposure: card balances are sensitive to unemployment and household finances, and fee revenue in wealth management falls if markets decline. The consumer figures were also supported by the credit picture described below, with charge-offs lower than a year earlier despite the larger loan book. The provision for credit losses was about two point seven billion dollars, compared with about three point four billion dollars a year earlier. That amount included roughly two point two billion dollars of net charge-offs, which were down about three hundred eighty-nine million dollars from the prior-year quarter, and a reserve build of about five hundred thirty-nine million dollars. According to published reports, the reserve build was mainly in wholesale lending. Lower charge-offs indicate that borrowers, on balance, continued to repay. The reserve build points in a slightly different direction: it shows that the bank is setting aside more against possible later losses in commercial portfolios, a decision driven by loan growth and by the bank's view of the economic path. Such builds can reflect prudence rather than deterioration, but they also acknowledge uncertainty. Wholesale credit has drawn attention across the industry this year because of questions about lending to nonbank financial companies and about the strength of some commercial borrowers. The JPMorgan release, as summarized in published reports, did not single out a specific problem exposure in this quarter, so the reserve addition should be read as a general provisioning step. For stock owners and for regulators, the balance between low realized losses and rising reserves is an important gauge. If charge-offs begin to rise while reserves have already been built, the cushion would be available; if charge-offs stay low, the reserve may eventually be released, which would boost reported earnings in a later period. The standardized common equity tier one ratio was an estimated thirteen point nine percent, and the advanced-approaches ratio was an estimated fourteen point one percent. Common equity tier one capital was about three hundred four billion dollars. These ratios remain well above the regulatory minimums the bank must satisfy, though the exact requirement includes buffers that regulators set for the largest banks. The company paid about four point four billion dollars in common dividends, or one dollar and sixty-five cents per share. Net share retirement spending were about six hundred sixty-four million dollars, a deliberately reduced pace compared with recent quarters. Mr. Dimon said the firm believes it can deploy the capital over time at very attractive rates of earnings for its stock owners, which signals that management is prepared to keep capital for balance-sheet growth, acquisitions or other uses rather than retiring shares at the earlier pace. A slower share retirement program can be read in several ways. It may reflect elevated stock prices, a wish to preserve flexibility ahead of regulatory capital changes, or an expectation of strong loan demand. The company did not give a single reason in the portions of the release that were reviewed for this article. The pace matters because retiring shares reduces the count over which earnings are spread. With the program slowed, per-share growth leans more heavily on underlying earnings growth. The pre-tax securities loss of about six hundred fifty-eight million dollars reduced reported earnings and explains the gap between the headline figure and the adjusted one. Published summaries did not describe the specific securities involved in the portions reviewed, and the filing treats the item as separate from the core run rate, which is why management presents results both with and without it. Noninterest expenses were about twenty-seven point three billion dollars, up about twelve percent from a year earlier. That growth rate exceeded the roughly eight percent rise in managed revenue, so the bank's operating efficiency was slightly weaker than a year ago on this measure. Compensation tied to strong trading and advisory revenue, technology spending and costs linked to business growth are the usual drivers, and published reports noted that some observers tied part of the increase to the stronger-than-expected revenue. The higher full-year expense guidance reinforces that cost growth is a live topic. Market participants often compare the pace of expense growth with revenue growth to judge operating leverage, meaning how much additional revenue translates into additional earnings. None of this changes the headline that the quarter was strong, but it shows where the pressure points sit: a one-time loss on the securities book, a rising reserve and costs that are growing faster than revenue. Whether those items fade or persist in coming quarters will shape how the full-year numbers look. JPMorgan reports alongside a group of large lenders whose results often move together. Goldman Sachs reported a sharp rise in equities revenue, and Charles Schwab reported record client asset gathering in the same period. The common thread is strong market activity, which lifted trading, brokerage and advisory lines across the sector. JPMorgan's distinguishing feature is breadth. title: J.P. Morgan Names Former Merrill Manager to Lead Southeast Market - AdvisorHub
content: Over a year after leaving thundering herd as part of a reorganization, former Merrill Lynch Private Wealth regional leader Linda A. Patel has returned to management at J.P. Morgan Advisors, the New York bank’s traditional brokerage unit. Linda A. Patel, who previously oversaw Merrill’s ultra-high net worth brokers in Texas, joined J.P. Morgan Advisors as head of its Southeast territory based in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, according to an announcement on Tuesday. Patel oversees around 80 advisors in Palm Beach Gardens, Palm Beach, Boca Raton, Miami and Atlanta, according to the announcement. She reports to J.P. Morgan Advisors Head Mollie Colavita and succeeds Janet Sweeney, a 40-year industry veteran who retired earlier this year. Sweeny had joined J.P. Morgan through its 2023 acquisition of First Republic Bank’s wealth unit. The appointment comes a little over a week after two of J.P. Morgan’s largest teams, who had generated $130 million in combined revenue from $18.6 billion in assets, left to launch RIA Latigo Peak Partners based in Palm Beach Gardens. “The Southeast continues to attract individuals, families and businesses with increasingly complex financial needs – creating significant opportunity for us to build on our strength in the region and grow alongside our clients,” Colavita said in a statement. Patel was one of two Merrill Private Wealth leaders who left in July 2025 as the firm consolidated six regions to four. She had led its Texas region since 2018 after overseeing offices in Thousand Oaks, California. Patel started her career at UBS’s PaineWebber predecessor in 1998 and joined Merrill through a predecessor later that year, according to BrokerCheck. For 55 years, On Lok has supported older adults across the Bay Area in accessing care and aging on their own terms. See how J.P. Morgan is backing On Lok’s next chapter with capital, expertise and a long-term relationship that goes beyond banking. In Cantonese, “On Lok” means happy, peaceful abode or home. The name carries both aspiration and promise, and, for more than five decades, the San Francisco nonprofit it describes has worked to make that promise real for thousands of older adults across the Bay Area. In 1971, a group of community members in San Francisco’s Chinatown North Beach neighborhood asked a deceptively simple question: Why should a person spend the final years of their life in a nursing home, far from the streets they walked, the food they loved and the language they spoke? Their answer: They shouldn’t. And that’s how On Lok was founded. For too many Americans, aging with dignity remains harder than it should be: Healthcare is fragmented, costs are rising and families navigate a maze of providers and social services. On Lok was built to meet that need. Problem: On Lok needed to open two new 23,000-square-foot centers in Union City and South San Jose simultaneously, while continuing to serve thousands of seniors across its existing programs, with complex multi-year financing needs that exceeded typical nonprofit banking. Solution: J.P. Morgan structured a $55 million direct purchase bond facility, drawing on its healthcare sector expertise to deliver creative, long-term financing. The firm complemented it with treasury management, healthcare payments technology and enterprise resource planning integration support to modernize On Lok’s operations at scale. Outcome: Both centers opened and have been fully operational since February 2026, expanding access to coordinated senior care for an estimated 800 additional seniors across the Bay Area. “It’s been 55 years now that On Lok has been part of this community,” said CEO Grace Li, who’s been with the organization for 25 years. “It came to be when members of our community recognized that the seniors in the Chinatown North Beach community really needed a way to receive care that was going to keep them close to their communities.” What emerged was the Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly—known as PACE—a coordinated, community-based alternative to nursing home placement that integrates medical care, social services, nutrition, transportation and daily activities under one roof. As On Lok proved the model locally, its leaders wanted to test whether it could work beyond San Francisco. They took the concept to the federal government as a demonstration and established a unique way to finance the program through Medicare and Medicaid to deliver the full range of services seniors need to stay in their communities. With grant support, On Lok worked with six organizations in six states to teach the approach and show it could deliver quality care beyond a single city or population. That proof helped pave the way for a permanent funding framework within Medicare regulations. Today, PACE operates in 33 states and the District of Columbia, serving more than 100,000 people. With approximately $286 million in annual revenue and more than 1,200 employees, On Lok is also a significant economic anchor in the San Francisco Bay Area, contracting with local vendors and generating the institutional stability that keeps neighborhoods viable. “Organizations don’t shape policy and change payment reform by accident,” Li said. “Being a local nonprofit where people see our vans and know who On Lok is—they just know.” “People can still make their own choices. It’s not easy to age and On Lok has been thinking about what our community members need as they age for 55 years.” On Lok’s services span a continuum of aging: active seniors come to senior centers for exercise, art, computer labs and communal meals; those with more complex needs receive care management and help navigating insurance and housing; and for seniors whose chronic conditions make daily life genuinely difficult, the PACE program provides fully integrated medical and social support that keeps them in the community rather than in institutional care. “On Lok’s mission is the voice of aging,” said Nicole Torres, COO and a 24-year member of the organization. Torres began her career as a nurse—starting in pediatrics at Lucile Packard at Stanford—before shifting into older-adult care and joining On Lok as a home care nurse. “We are serving people who are yearning to age as they want to age. We are also serving communities that need us, who are vulnerable, who are unheard.” Marie, a pianist and PACE participant at the On Lok 30th Street Center, came to On Lok after breaking her femur during the pandemic. Today she plays piano for fellow participants several times a week. “I kept hoping I could play music for people again. The dream came true,” Marie said. She is also grateful for the healthcare support: “It’s a lifesaver for me.” Jeffrey, a 66-year-old former cable linesman and self-taught artist at the On Lok PACE South San Jose Center, has had his drawings celebrated by staff and shared with other participants. “The medical support here is impressive,” he said. “I thought I was at the end of my rope. It makes me feel like I’m still somebody. On Lok takes good care of me.” On Lok’s reach is deeply local: It employs physicians, nurses, social workers, therapists, drivers and nutritionists, and contracts with local small businesses and community providers. Its impact extends far beyond its walls, strengthening families, caregivers and the community institutions that make neighborhoods work. That’s the lens JPMorganChase applies through the American Dream Initiative: scaling proven local solutions by mobilizing capital, know-how and practical policy support alongside local organizations. The initiative was designed, in part, to finance local healthcare infrastructure that expands opportunity. For aging Americans, that opportunity means staying in your neighborhood, maintaining independence and receiving high-quality care without being uprooted from everything you know. “The work we do addresses healthcare, medical care and social supports for that senior and its impact goes beyond the senior,” Torres said. “It helps their community, the immediate caregivers, the friends, the daughters, the husband, the wife and then it helps the greater neighborhood.” Connect with our team to learn how J.P. Morgan can support your mission-driven organization in strengthening operations, accessing capital and scaling community impact. On Lok made what Torres calls “a bold move”: opening two brand-new PACE centers simultaneously, one in Union City and one in South San Jose, each spanning approximately 23,000 square feet with a full primary care clinic and adult day health center, while continuing to operate all existing programs at capacity. “J.P. Morgan is the expert at banking and financial services. On Lok is not. We had to recognize who are experts in helping organizations think about how to scale.” J.P. Morgan provided a $55 million direct purchase bond facility to finance the acquisition and development of both sites, a transaction requiring careful multi-year planning and deep sector-specific expertise. “For this particular financing opportunity, we turned to J.P. Morgan and talked with them about ways that they could help support us,” Li said. “J.P. Morgan helped us with a huge historic endeavor,” Torres said. “After two years plus of blood, sweat and tears, those buildings are fully built out and we’ve been operational since February.” For Stu Bessieres, Relationship Executive at J.P. Morgan, the milestone is personal. “On Lok is a critical organization of San Francisco that represents our true San Franciscan identity. J.P. Morgan was integral in providing the capital necessary for On Lok to expand in both their Union City and South San Jose locations. I saw the buses driving around growing up. Now I get to truly be a part of its success.” J.P. Morgan is supporting On Lok’s migration to an enterprise resource planning (ERP) platform, transitioning reconciliation and payment origination from manual to fully automated processes. The migration is expected to be completed by the end of 2026. $56M in payments processed via InstaMed by J.P. Morgan InstaMed (over a 12-month period) The relationship extends into sector connectivity: J.P. Morgan has brought On Lok into its annual Healthcare Conference, nonprofit roundtables and webinars. Employees also volunteer directly at On Lok, playing bingo with participants and tending the center’s garden. On Lok’s story is, at its core, a story about generations. The organization is now serving the children and grandchildren of the first seniors it cared for in 1971. That generational continuity is both a measure of past success and a mandate for what comes next. “We’re already serving generations of families,” Li said. “There are grandkids who always would come and know On Lok because they visited their grandparent here or their parent here.” Torres looks ahead with clarity. “The next 55 years look bright. Tenfold the lives that we’re serving now. Double, tripling our workforce. Continuing to build our relationships and synergies with community organizations and institutions like J.P. Morgan.” The two new centers in Union City and South San Jose are not endpoints. They are, as Torres frames it, a signal that a longstanding nonprofit can keep growing, innovating and making room for more people to age with dignity and connection. “The opportunity to have the support of J.P. Morgan, our community partners, the staff that come to work every day to do this mission-driven work—we’re just grateful,” Li said. title: JPMorgan Chase Says That Bitcoin Will Outperform Stocks, Bonds, and Gold Over the Next 10 Years. Here's Why It Might Be Right - The Motley Fool
content: The banking giant is still pretty skeptical about Bitcoin. Per a new report, the asset management arm of JPMorgan Chase (JPM +1.04%) has a base case in which Bitcoin (BTC -1.20%) beats domestic stocks, bonds, and even gold during the next 10 years. It expects the crypto to return 10% annually during that period, versus 7.5% for U.S. large-cap stocks, 5.6% for broad U.S. bonds, and 5.5% for gold. It's the first time the report has put a range on Bitcoin's returns, and it comes with a handful of heavy caveats. Although the figures it calculated are unlikely to prove true in 2036, the drivers for those results are hard to argue against, and it's my view that JPMorgan Chase is directionally correct. Here's why. The JPMorgan Chase report is largely about the investing implications of the macroeconomic conditions facing the world during the coming years, touching on everything from inflation to global warming and, of course, Bitcoin. It expects artificial-intelligence-driven productivity gains to push the U.S. economy's real growth rate to 2.1% annually, with inflation averaging 2.4% in the same period. It also raised its expected annual return for large companies, such as those in the S&P 500 index, from 6.7% to 7.5%, citing strong profit margins. But it contends that Bitcoin will be buoyed by three different factors that will offer better performance than this. The most important driver, with a 65% weight in the calculation, is Bitcoin's slowing supply growth relative to global money growth. The second-most-important factor, with a weight of 30%, is Bitcoin's inclusion in portfolios alongside allocations to other scarce store-of-value assets, such as gold. The last driver is the weakest: the coin's increasing network activity. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » The bank's estimated growth rate for its base case implies that Bitcoin would be priced at about $211,130 by 2036. Its bear case, which calls for an 11.2% annual loss, implies a price of about $24,817, roughly 70% below its $81,300 level as of Oct. 26. The bull case would see it grow by 16.6% annually. But no matter which of those scenarios plays out, the bank expects the coin's volatility to be 55%, based on historical data. Overall, JPMorgan Chase's projections for Bitcoin's price growth are on the bearish side compared to Bitcoin's history, but they look reasonable. The coin has a 10-year compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 63%. The supply model is difficult to dispute; Bitcoin's next halving, when the number of new coins miners earn per block is halved, is expected sometime in April 2028. The U.S. M2, one gauge of the broad money supply, grew by 5.7% in the year through August 2026. The bank doubts that a currency-debasement scare will spark a rush into crypto, but its model doe assumes a modest shift. Its projected inflation during the next decade is significantly lower than September 2026's 3.7% annual pace, which means that if inflation remains elevated, the importance of Bitcoin as a potential hedge against it could drive its performance toward the bull case. Still, the bank calls the coin "a speculative asset and a hedge against monetary easing." It says volatility has declined, but unstable correlations make Bitcoin premature as a diversifier. Though JPMorgan Chase still doesn't recommend buying Bitcoin, it probably makes sense to own at least a little to gain exposure to its upside in the bank's base case, and perhaps a bit more upside if the bull case plays out. HSBC launched its Hong Kong dollar-denominated stablecoin, RedCoin, on 23 October through PayMe, with wallet activation rolling out to more than 3.3 million users and payments supported at more than 100,000 merchants. The launch implements the initial peer-to-peer and merchant-payment phase outlined on 30 September. HSBC plans to add mobile banking wallet functionality and tokenised investment subscriptions later this year, including a planned share class of its HKD money market fund, with corporate and institutional applications also planned. RedCoin initially operates within HSBC-controlled infrastructure, with wider blockchain connectivity dependent on further regulatory approval. It runs on a private, permissioned blockchain operated by HSBC; public-chain connectivity would require HKMA approval. RedCoin is backed by segregated HKD reserve assets and redeemable at par, but pays no interest and is not covered by Hong Kong’s Deposit Protection Scheme. Rival Anchorpoint began rolling out HKDAP in August through distributors serving institutional, corporate and professional-investor markets. JP Morgan Payments and the Asian Development Bank announced on 22 October an expanded collaboration to broaden access to working capital for businesses across India through a risk-sharing framework. The arrangement covers trade and working-capital finance across supply chains, including financing for manufacturers, buyers and suppliers. Target sectors include food, pharmaceuticals, electric vehicles and renewable energy. The collaboration builds on a longstanding relationship. In 2017, ADB and JP Morgan introduced a funded risk-sharing product expected to support more than $100 million in trade across developing Asia. The latest announcement extends their cooperation to Indian corporates and their supply chains. ADB’s guarantee transfers part of the credit risk on eligible exposures, potentially enabling JP Morgan to finance transactions that would otherwise be constrained by its credit limits or risk appetite. Ripple launched new capabilities for Ripple Treasury on 26 October, connecting cash positioning, forecasting, reconciliation, liquidity management and payments. The platform includes 24/7 Returns, which allows eligible corporate customers to generate returns on qualifying digital assets held in a Ripple wallet, including Ripple’s dollar-backed stablecoin RLUSD, subject to programme requirements. Ripple says customers can put eligible assets to work outside traditional banking hours without managing the underlying digital-asset transactions themselves. The announcement builds on Ripple’s $1 billion GTreasury acquisition, announced in October 2025, and September’s expansion of GSmart’s treasury AI capabilities. The announcement does not specify the underlying return-generating strategy, which corporate treasury teams would need to assess alongside access to liquidity and investment policies. The Monetary Authority of Singapore announced on 23 October that Bank Negara Malaysia and the Bank of Thailand had joined BLOOM as policymaker members. Participants are developing common arrangements for accepting, exchanging and settling tokenised deposits and regulated stablecoins across jurisdictions, including contractual arrangements, identity verification and sanctions controls. MAS says this could reduce the separate agreements and integrations financial institutions need for each counterparty or market. Under BLOOM, Ripple announced a pilot with trade finance technology provider Unloq in March using RLUSD to release trade payments when predefined conditions, such as shipment verification, are met. Visa announced a pilot with Nium in August, also under BLOOM, to explore stablecoin settlement across weekends and public holidays. These applications depend on receiving institutions being able to recognise, accept and settle the digital money under their own regulatory and operating requirements. BLOOM’s common arrangements seek to address those requirements across jurisdictions. TerraPay announced on 22 October that it had integrated its Verify payee-verification service with JP Morgan’s Kinexys Liink Confirm application. The integration allows banks and non-bank financial institutions connected to Liink, as well as TerraPay Verify clients, to validate recipient bank-account and digital-wallet details across global markets before initiating payments. The service targets payment failures caused by inaccurate beneficiary information, adding TerraPay’s verification coverage to Confirm’s existing account-validation capabilities. Checking recipient details before funds move can reduce rejected payments and the manual work needed to investigate and resubmit them. The announcement establishes expanded verification access, but provides no measured reduction in payment failures or fraud. Visa announced enhanced commercial payment capabilities on 21 October, including supplier-spend analytics, virtual-card fraud controls and a live invoice-payment pilot with BILL and Billtrust first announced the previous day. In the pilot, an authorised AI agent initiates and completes approved invoice payments through supplier portals using tokenised credentials and buyer-defined controls. Visa said end-to-end transactions were being processed with participating BILL customers and Billtrust suppliers. The pilot extends Visa’s Trusted Agent Protocol, introduced with partners in October 2025, into business invoice payments across buyer and supplier platforms. Billtrust authenticates the agent accessing the supplier portal, allowing it to complete an approved payment without shared supplier login credentials. The buyer retains payment approval authority while the agent carries out the portal interaction. Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC) and Ant International signed a memorandum of understanding on 26 October to collaborate on cross-border payments and transaction flows involving Japan, Singapore and Southeast Asia. SMBC will support Ant International’s Alipay+, Antom and WorldFirst businesses with payments and treasury management. The parties will also explore integrating Ant’s Whale RTP platform with SMBC’s digital payment and asset solutions to support intercompany treasury and global liquidity management. Ant has already pursued related treasury initiatives with other banks, including DBS’s treasury-token pilot and Standard Chartered’s HKD blockchain test settlement. On 7 October, OCBC announced a tokenised-deposit service enabling Ant to manage liquidity between Singapore and Malaysia around the clock. SMBC’s agreement adds another potential banking connection to that network, although its proposed technical integration remains exploratory. Ping An Digital Bank launched Receivables Financing and Invoice Financing on 21 October for Hong Kong importers and exporters, offering revolving facilities of up to HKD 50 million ($6.4 million). Exporters can obtain advances against outstanding receivables using commercial invoices and bills of lading, while importers can have approved financing paid directly to suppliers, with repayment terms of three to six months. The bank says digital drawdowns can provide funds in as little as one business day. The products extend an offering that includes purchase-order financing and cross-border e-commerce revolving loans. They address different points in the trade cash cycle: exporters obtain liquidity while awaiting customer payments, while importers finance supplier payments before generating sales proceeds. For its existing Trade-Connect loans, the bank also uses consenting Tradelink customers’ trade-declaration data to support credit assessment. The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development renewed its Regional Trade Facilitation Programme on 21 October, with a maximum outstanding amount of EUR 4.5 billion ($5.1 billion). The programme provides guarantees covering payment risk on trade-finance instruments issued by participating banks and factors, as well as revolving cash advances that allow participating institutions to finance exporters and importers. The programme began in 1999 and was previously renewed in February 2025. At the end of 2025, more than 140 banks and factoring companies in 27 EBRD countries of operation were accredited, while more than 800 banks in 82 countries participated as confirming banks. The renewal maintains this established channel connecting local trade lenders with international confirming institutions. The African Development Bank approved a EUR 40 million ($44.9 million) facility for AFG Bank Cameroon on 21 October, comprising a EUR 30 million ($33.7 million) trade-finance credit line over 3.5 years and a EUR 10 million ($11.2 million) transaction guarantee facility over five years. The guarantee can provide up to 100% coverage to confirming banks for eligible letters of credit and similar trade-finance instruments issued by AFG Bank Cameroon. Half of the credit line is earmarked for SMEs, with 30% of that SME allocation directed to women- or youth-owned enterprises. The credit line funds AFG’s trade lending, while the guarantee covers eligible payment risk faced by confirming banks. Providing liquidity to the issuing bank alone does not remove that risk. The facility extends an approach AfDB has also used with Cameroon’s CCA-Bank, whose earlier package combined a trade credit line with a transaction guarantee. © Copyright 2026, The Asian Banker. JPMorgan Chase's (NYSE: JPM) asset management division recently released the 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions report, an annual research report that includes 10- to 15-year return projections. For the first time, it has a returns forecast for Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC), and expects the top cryptocurrency to outperform the major asset classes. It's another sign of the growing acceptance of cryptocurrency. CEO Jamie Dimon previously called Bitcoin a fraud, and as recently as 2025, he said he didn't see its value. However, a positive forecast doesn't necessarily mean Bitcoin is a slam-dunk investment. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » JPMorgan's base case for Bitcoin is 10% annualized returns over the next 10 to 15 years, but the bank sees a wide range of potential returns. Its bear case is -11.2%, and its bull case is about 16.5%. For perspective, JPMorgan forecasts annualized returns of 7.5% for U.S. large-cap stocks, 7.7% for small-cap stocks, 5.5% for gold, and 5.6% to 6.6% for U.S. bonds. Real estate investment trusts (REITs) came in at 8.2%. If JPMorgan's base cases are accurate, $100 invested in Bitcoin would grow to $259 over the next 10 years. The same amount invested in large caps would grow to $206. The press release for JPMorgan's report specifically noted that Bitcoin isn't included as an allocation. The bank also hasn't yet included Bitcoin in its main covariance matrices, the models it uses to determine how much of an asset belongs in a portfolio. JPMorgan laid out two obstacles to Bitcoin portfolio use: volatility and unstable correlations with other assets. Cryptocurrency is known for its volatility, and in Bitcoin's case, JPMorgan assumes 55% annualized volatility, compared to 18% for U.S. large caps and 17.2% for gold. This volatility is why there's such a large gap between the bull and bear cases for Bitcoin. In the bear case, where Bitcoin loses 11.2% per year, you'd end up with roughly 30% of your money after 10 years. Bitcoin's unstable correlations with other assets make it difficult to allocate in a portfolio. You can't count on it as a hedge or to balance out risk, because even though it's sometimes called "digital gold," Bitcoin doesn't perform that way. Gold has held its value during several stock sell-offs, whereas Bitcoin frequently falls with the stock market. A small position in Bitcoin is worth considering if you have a high tolerance for risk and volatility. The cryptocurrency has historically outperformed stocks by a wide margin during its bull markets, with the trade-off that it suffers much greater losses during bear markets. As of Oct. 26, with Bitcoin trading about 36% below the all-time high it set in October 2025, investors can buy in well below its peak. It's not a must-have, though -- investing in stocks is the far more proven option, and you don't need Bitcoin to get market-beating returns. Even JPMorgan considers Bitcoin a speculative asset, and its bear case shows the potential downside. If you decide to buy Bitcoin, a sensible approach is to limit it to about 5% of your portfolio.
